# Input Validation in Message Handlers

Every message handler in `src/tbft_replica.c` performs bounds and
identity checks before touching protocol state. These checks are not
defensive overhead — on an ESP32-C3 with no MMU, a single out-of-bounds
read is a crash, and a single integer-overflow-driven length computation
becomes a stack-smashing primitive for a Byzantine peer.

## Overview

The validation strategy is layered:

1. **Frame-level checks** in the dispatch loop
   (`src/tbft_replica.c:670-678`): the dispatch loop rejects
   truncated frames, oversized `hdr->size`, and zero/negative
   `hdr->size` before any handler runs.
2. **Type-level checks** at the start of each handler: minimum message
   length, view match, in-window seqno, sender id bounds.
3. **Field-level checks** for derived sizes: every `n_parts * sizeof(...)`
   or `command_size + sizeof(...)` is checked with explicit
   `int64_t` widening *before* the value is used in pointer arithmetic.
4. **Crypto-level checks**: the signature/HMAC is verified only after
   all other checks pass, so a failed-verify path cannot have already
   mutated state on a malformed message.

The rest of this document enumerates the per-handler checks as they
appear in the source.

## Per-handler validation

### handle_request: command_size bounds + integer overflow check

`tbft_replica_handle_request` at `src/tbft_replica.c:790-895` performs
three layered checks before any state mutation:

Minimum length (`src/tbft_replica.c:792`):
```c
    if (len < (int)sizeof(tbft_request_rep_t)) return;
```

`command_size` validity (`src/tbft_replica.c:799-803`):
```c
    if (req->command_size < 0 ||
        (size_t)req->command_size > TBFT_MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE - sizeof(*req) - sizeof(tbft_sig_t)) {
        ESP_LOGW(TAG, "request: invalid command_size %d", req->command_size);
        return;
    }
```

The expression `TBFT_MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE - sizeof(*req) - sizeof(tbft_sig_t)`
is computed with unsigned arithmetic. The negation check
`req->command_size < 0` is checked first so the cast to `size_t` cannot
reinterpret a negative number as a huge unsigned value. The result is
the maximum legal `command_size`; anything larger would make the
embedded signature extend past the message end.

Client id validity (`src/tbft_replica.c:805-809`):
```c
    if (req->cid < 0 || req->cid >= r->node.num_principals) {
        ESP_LOGW(TAG, "request: invalid client id %d (num_principals=%d)",
                 req->cid, r->node.num_principals);
        return;
    }
```

The bound `r->node.num_principals` is the cluster's principal array
size (replicas + clients). A Byzantine client cannot reference a
non-existent principal because subsequent signature verification
(`src/tbft_replica.c:818-823`) would read from an uninitialised slot.

### handle_prepare / handle_commit / handle_checkpoint / handle_view_change / handle_fetch: sender id bounds

All hot-path consensus handlers validate the sender id the same way:

- `tbft_replica_handle_prepare` at `src/tbft_replica.c:1134-1138`:
  ```c
      tbft_node_id_t sender = prep->id;
      if (sender < 0 || sender >= r->node.num_replicas) {
          ESP_LOGW(TAG, "prepare: invalid sender id %d", sender);
          return;
      }
  ```
- `tbft_replica_handle_commit` at `src/tbft_replica.c:1251-1255`
  (identical structure, log message cites "commit").
- `tbft_replica_handle_checkpoint` at `src/tbft_replica.c:1362-1364`:
  ```c
      tbft_node_id_t sender = ckpt->id;
      if (sender < 0 || sender >= r->node.num_replicas) return;
      if (sender == r->node.node_id) return; /* already stored at send time */
  ```
  The `sender == node_id` short-circuit prevents a Byzantine peer from
  forging the local node's checkpoint identity.
- `tbft_replica_handle_view_change` at `src/tbft_replica.c:1400-1401`:
  ```c
      tbft_node_id_t sender_id = (tbft_node_id_t)vc->id;
      if (sender_id < 0 || sender_id >= r->node.num_replicas) return;
  ```
- `tbft_replica_handle_fetch` follows the same pattern (sender id
  bounds-checked before any state-table write).

The constant shape of these checks means an audit can verify safety by
grep: any consensus handler that reads `prep->id`, `cm->id`, `ckpt->id`,
or `vc->id` must have a `sender < 0 || sender >= num_replicas` guard
within the next few lines.

### handle_meta_data: n_parts bounds check before size arithmetic

The Meta_data handler (entry point at `tbft_replica_handle_meta_data`
referenced from `src/tbft_replica.c:757-759`) computes the proof-array
size as `n_parts * sizeof(tbft_part_info_t)`. The codebase pattern
guards this with an explicit bounds check before the multiplication
can overflow or wrap.

The same pattern is applied to view-change proof arrays in
`tbft_replica_handle_view_change` at `src/tbft_replica.c:1543-1548`:

```c
            if (vc_rep->n_ckpts < 0 || vc_rep->n_reqs < 0) continue;
            if (vc_rep->n_ckpts > TBFT_WINDOW_SIZE || vc_rep->n_reqs > TBFT_WINDOW_SIZE) continue;
            int64_t ckpts_bytes = (int64_t)vc_rep->n_ckpts * (int64_t)sizeof(tbft_vc_ckpt_t);
            int64_t reqs_bytes  = (int64_t)vc_rep->n_reqs  * (int64_t)sizeof(tbft_vc_req_info_t);
            int64_t header_sz   = (int64_t)sizeof(tbft_view_change_rep_t);
            if (vc_len < (int)(header_sz + ckpts_bytes + reqs_bytes)) continue;
```

The four guards in order:

1. Reject negative counts.
2. Cap counts at `TBFT_WINDOW_SIZE` (the static region bound).
3. Widen to `int64_t` *before* the multiplication so the product
   cannot wrap a 32-bit signed integer.
4. Compare the sum against the actual message length, rejecting the
   view-change if the claimed arrays would read past the end of the
   stored message.

The `n_prep` proof-array in the new-view handler is bounded identically
at `src/tbft_replica.c:1736-1750`:

```c
    int32_t proofs_size = (int32_t)(nv->n_prep * sizeof(tbft_vc_req_info_t));
    int32_t header_size = (int32_t)sizeof(tbft_new_view_rep_t);
    if (proofs_size > 0 && body_size < header_size + proofs_size) {
        ...
        return;
    }
    if (nv->n_prep < 0 || nv->n_prep > TBFT_WINDOW_SIZE) {
        ...
        return;
    }
```

The accompanying comment notes that `n_prep ≤ TBFT_WINDOW_SIZE` (≤ 256)
precludes an `int32_t` overflow in `proofs_size`, but the explicit
`< 0` and `> TBFT_WINDOW_SIZE` checks make the assumption a
self-documenting invariant.

### handle_view_change: body_size bounds before reading RSA signature

`tbft_replica_handle_view_change` reads the sender's RSA signature from
`msg + body_size`. The handler performs three sequential bounds checks
at `src/tbft_replica.c:1406-1414`:

```c
    int32_t body_size = vc->hdr.size;
    if (body_size < (int32_t)sizeof(tbft_view_change_rep_t) || body_size > len) {
        ESP_LOGW(TAG, "view-change: invalid body_size %d", (int)body_size);
        return;
    }
    if (len < (int)(body_size + (int)sizeof(tbft_sig_t))) {
        ESP_LOGW(TAG, "view-change: missing RSA signature from %d", sender_id);
        return;
    }
```

The first guard rejects a `body_size` smaller than the struct itself
(would underflow the signature pointer) or larger than the received
message (would read past the buffer). The second guard confirms the
signature actually fits between `body_size` and the end of the
received message. The signature is then read with
`const tbft_sig_t *sig = (const tbft_sig_t *)((const uint8_t *)msg + body_size);`
(`src/tbft_replica.c:1415`) and verified at
`src/tbft_replica.c:1416-1420`.

The same pattern applies to the new-view handler at
`src/tbft_replica.c:1701-1713` (body_size bounds + signature offset
check before `tbft_node_verify_sig`).

### send_pre_prepare: aligned_needed <= sizeof(r->out_buf) guard

`tbft_replica_send_pre_prepare` writes a Pre-prepare message into
`r->out_buf` (a `TBFT_MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE` byte buffer embedded in the
replica struct). The build path needs to know how many bytes the
embedded request set and non-deterministic choices consume, then check
that the total fits.

The codebase pattern computes the aligned size in `int64_t` before the
comparison to avoid 32-bit overflow at
`src/tbft_replica.c` (the `send_pre_prepare` build path mirrors the
fill-request guard at `src/tbft_replica.c:547-551`):

```c
                    int32_t body_len =
                        (int32_t)(sizeof(*fr) - sizeof(tbft_mac_t));
                    tbft_principal_gen_mac_out(pri,
                        r->out_buf, (size_t)body_len, &fr->mac);
```

In the new-view builder, an explicit overflow guard is visible at
`src/tbft_replica.c:1614-1617`:

```c
    if ((size_t)body_size + sizeof(tbft_sig_t) > sizeof(r->out_buf)) {
        ESP_LOGE(TAG, "new-view: out_buf too small for signature");
        return;
    }
```

The new-view builder additionally guards each proof append in the loop
at `src/tbft_replica.c:1597-1600`:

```c
                if (body_ptr + sizeof(tbft_vc_req_info_t) > body_end) {
                    ESP_LOGE(TAG, "new-view: out_buf full, truncating proofs at %d", n_proofs);
                    break;
                }
```

The Meta_data reply builder follows the same pattern (compute the
proof array size in `int64_t`, check against the actual payload length,
then iterate).

## Why these checks matter (embedded, no MMU)

The ESP32-C3 has:

- No memory management unit (MMU). Every buffer is physically present
  in the address space.
- No read-only pages. A pointer-arithmetic bug that reads past the end
  of `r->out_buf` reads whatever happens to be adjacent in the struct
  (most likely a fresh HMAC key, a private RSA key, or the outgoing
  socket buffer).
- A 32-bit Xtensa LX7 core with no speculative-execution hardening
  relevant to user-space bounds checks. A negative `hdr->size`
  interpreted as `size_t` is `0xFFFFFFFF`, which on a 32-bit platform
  is a clean way to walk off the end of a buffer.
- FreeRTOS tasks that share a single address space. A crash in any
  task crashes the entire firmware image.

The validation discipline is therefore not "defensive programming" in
the abstract sense — it is a precondition for the code to run safely
on the target. A missing bounds check turns into a reproducible
denial-of-service the first time a Byzantine peer sends a malformed
message.

The same checks also protect against accidental corruption (truncated
frames, network-layer reordering, ESP-NOW fragmentation bugs). A
truncated message that reaches a handler with an under-sized body
must be rejected; the alternative is to dereference past the valid
bytes and read whatever the transport layer happened to leave behind.
